title: Load a trailer with 60% of the weight ahead of the axle
instruction: Load all three crates onto the trailer bed so that at least 60% of their total weight is ahead of the axle (the red line), on the hitch side. The grey steel crate weighs 160 g and each wooden crate 40 g.
context: Movers, landscapers and anyone towing a trailer load at least 60% of the cargo weight ahead of the axle; a tail-heavy trailer sways and can jackknife. Here only the steel crate's side of the axle decides it, so the robot has to reason about weight, not just fill the bed.
setup: A wooden table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A fixed flatbed trailer: wooden bed 240 x 60 x 20 mm, long side running side to side, centred 330 mm forward and on the midline; its black tongue and hitch point left. A 6 mm red stripe across the bed, 20 mm right of its centre, marks the axle, with a black wheel block (14 x 44 x 44 mm) on each side. Three 40 mm cube crates stand on the table 220 mm forward: a grey sheet-steel crate (160 g) 150 mm left, a brown wooden crate (40 g) 50 mm left and another (40 g) 120 mm right.
scoring: A crate counts as on the bed when it stands flat on it (centre within 4 mm of its resting height, tilted under 5 degrees) with its whole footprint over the bed. 0.2 per crate on the bed; plus 0.4 if all three are on it and the crates whose centres are on the hitch side of the axle line's centre make up at least 60% of the total weight (160 + 40 + 40 g). Success once the score is 1.0 and all crates are still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift the crates back to their start marks on the table; the trailer stays fixed.
fidelity: The trailer is fixed in place and doesn't tip or rest on its hitch, so weight ahead of the axle is judged from where the crates stand rather than from a tongue-weight reading. Crates are solid boxes with the stated masses; the trailer is scaled down to table size.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, no crate loaded); demo: 1.0
